the nuclear suppression of the open charm cross section at the LHC, as measured by CMS, is inconsistent with a simple scaling of the proton structure function, F 2 p ( x, Q 2 ).

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no evidence of a suppression in the nuclear gluon density at small x, but there is evidence that the nuclear parton distributions are not simply a convolution of nucleon distributions.
the factorization theorem of QCD is violated in charm hadro-production.
there is a breakdown of factorization in the nuclear case.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nuclear anomaly cannot be explained in a simple way.

the anomalous A dependence in J/ψ and D meson hadroproduction cannot arise from a modification in the nuclear gluon density, and that it is a consequence of the interplay of the gluon density and higher twist effects.
the nuclear anomaly in the J/ψ and the open charm production cannot be explained by gluon shadowing alone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nuclear anomaly in J/ψ production is not a problem of nuclear PDFs, but of the factorization formula for the production of heavy hadrons in hadronic collisions.
the factorization of the nuclear wave function from the partonic cross section breaks down for the nuclear target.
the factorization of the nuclear wave function is violated, and that the nuclear wave function must be treated nonperturbatively in QCD.
